paragraphs: Holly sells an AI-powered classification and compensation platform for government human resources departments. It is built for HR teams that manage hundreds of classifications, compete for talent and negotiate pay.

The platform scores an existing job spec for clarity, completeness and equity, calling out outdated duties, dense sentences or qualifications that screen out strong candidates. Its similarity scoring compares actual job duties across more than 45,000 public sector roles rather than titles alone. Drafts move through subject matter expert, HR, management and final approval steps, with reviewers commenting the way they would in a shared document. Market data is turned into recommendations for council meetings and union negotiations.

The users are local government HR staff, and one published case study follows Long Beach, California, a port city of about 450,000 residents. Its workforce numbers roughly 6,000 employees across close to 350 civil service classifications. Holly was started by Brendan Hellweg and Cherie Chung, who met as graduate students at Harvard Business School and Harvard Kennedy School. The company says it is supported by J2 Ventures, Roble Ventures, Gaingels and angel investors.

quote.text: Holly is an AI driven platform that helps local governments create more effective evidence based jobs.
